run.question: Search the 'app-183c-logs' index for ERROR level log messages. What error codes (format ERR-XXXX) appear in the logs?

report.summary: In the app-183c-logs index, three ERROR-level log documents fall inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T04:31:07Z to 2026-11-21T04:31:07Z, and they carry three distinct error codes in ERR-XXXX format: ERR-7291, ERR-4058 and ERR-9463, each appearing exactly once. The whole index held 7 documents in that window (3 ERROR, 1 WARN, 3 INFO), so these are the complete set of ERROR documents the index returned for that window, not a sample truncated by size. This was a log-content lookup, not a fault attribution: no root cause is asserted and no service is named as affected.

claims.text: The index app-183c-logs maps a date field named timestamp plus level, message, service and error_code (all keyword except message, which is text); it does not map @timestamp, so the timestamp field was used as the time filter.
At query time the index app-183c-logs was green/open with docs.count 7 and store.size 9.2kb.

An ERROR-level filter (term level=ERROR) over app-183c-logs returned total 3 documents, with documents_shown 3 and truncated false: 2026-11-21T04:09:00Z payment-api 'Database connection timeout - ERR-7291: Failed to connect to primary database after 30s'; 2026-11-21T04:14:00Z order-service 'Payment validation failed - ERR-4058: Invalid card number format'; 2026-11-21T04:24:00Z inventory-api 'Stock sync failed - ERR-9463: External inventory API returned 503'.

A match_all read of app-183c-logs sorted by timestamp returned all 7 documents in the window (04:04Z to 04:29Z) and truncated false: 3 ERROR, 1 WARN (04:10:00Z payment-api 'Retrying database connection'), and 3 INFO ('Service started successfully' 04:04Z payment-api, 'Processing order batch complete' 04:19Z order-service, 'Recovered from temporary outage' 04:29Z inventory-api); only the ERROR documents carry an error_code value.

A terms aggregation on error_code for level=ERROR returned exactly three buckets of doc_count 1 each: ERR-4058, ERR-7291 and ERR-9463, with sum_other_doc_count 0; the service aggregation matched them one-to-one with order-service, payment-api and inventory-api.

gaps: The index's document count is only 7, so the code list is complete for what this index holds in the 2026-11-20T04:31:07Z to 2026-11-21T04:31:07Z window, but it cannot show whether other ERR-XXXX codes occurred in logs this index does not retain (retention or ingest gaps are unknown).
Logs older than 2026-11-20T04:31:07Z or newer than 2026-11-21T04:31:07Z were not read; the newest returned document is 2026-11-21T04:29:00Z.

Whether these three ERR codes correspond to a live fault in payment-api, order-service or inventory-api was not investigated here; the request was a log content lookup, so no health assessment of those services is made and they are not classified as affected.
next_steps: If a fault assessment is wanted, correlate these timestamps (04:09Z, 04:14Z, 04:24Z) with per-service error-rate and latency metrics and traces for payment-api, order-service and inventory-api over the same window.
Confirm log retention and shipping coverage for app-183c-logs before treating the three codes as an exhaustive inventory of error codes for the period.
